entry.reasons: The definition of a parallel connection matches the CED statement 11.5.A.1.ii exactly: 'A parallel connection is one in which charges may flow through one of two or more paths. Across each path, the potential difference is the same.' The topic codes are appropriate as parallel connections are introduced in Topic 11.5 and are highly relevant to Kirchhoff's Junction Rule in Topic 11.7.

The entry accurately defines 'series connection' using the exact phrasing from Essential Knowledge 11.5.A.1.i ('A series connection is one in which any charge passing through one circuit element must proceed through all elements in that connection and has no other path available. The current in each element in series must be the same.').

The entry is factual and directly supported by the CED. Under Topic 11.8 (Resistor-Capacitor (RC) Circuits), Essential Knowledge 11.8.B.1.i defines the time constant as \tau = RC (or \tau = R_{eq}C_{eq} for combinations). The caution correctly notes that only qualitative descriptions of charging/discharging are required, as explicitly stated in the Topic 11.8 Boundary Statement: 'Descriptions of charging/discharging RC circuits in AP Physics 2 are limited to qualitative descriptions and representations... students are not expected to mathematically model these behaviors with respect to time.'

Topic 11.8 requires the RC time constant and states that it is defined by an equation (11.8.B.1.i); the equivalent-resistance and equivalent-capacitance form applies when those are the effective values for the RC circuit. The caution overstates the boundary by saying "Only qualitative use is required." The CED limits descriptions of charging and discharging over time to qualitative representations, but explicitly says students should be able to "mathematically describe initial and final states of RC circuits." Its restriction is that students are "not expected to mathematically model these behaviors with respect to time," not that all use of the time constant must be qualitative.

Topic 11.8 requires the RC time constant: 11.8.B.1.i says it measures how quickly a capacitor charges or discharges and gives its definition. But the entry presents τ = R_eq C_eq without restricting it to a circuit reducible to one equivalent resistance and capacitance; the CED does not state that as a general rule for every combination. The caution also overstates the boundary. The CED excludes mathematical modeling of charging and discharging *with respect to time*, not quantitative use of the time constant itself. Its 63% and 37% descriptions support the rest of the caution.
